items.title: Over a regular ring perfect modules are exactly the finite modules and perfect complexes are those with bounded finite cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes perfect objects over a regular ring in two forms: a module is perfect exactly when it is finite, and a complex is perfect exactly when it is bounded with finite cohomology (statement lines 19114-19122). The proof of the first part is a covering argument: taking a finite free resolution of a finite module, the loci where the successive syzygies are free form an increasing sequence of opens because projectivity over a local ring is freeness, the local rings being regular have finite global dimension so a large syzygy is free at each prime, and Noetherianity of the spectrum makes the cover stabilize at some finite stage, after which the truncated resolution exhibits the module as perfect (proof lines 19124-19161). The second part is then deduced from the first by applying it to each cohomology module of a bounded complex. The counted span refers to six labelled results of another chapter and to one criterion of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
